subject: Useful trick for compiling Stan models with debug info

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Useful trick for compiling Stan models with debug info
parts:
There is no obvious way, using the Stan make files, to compile a model with debug info so that you can run it under gdb. You can, of course, use make -n to see the commands that will be run and then modify them to include the -g flag, but that's a bit awkward. The make files do, however, allow you to explicitly set the optimization level; for example, you can do

    make O=0 <path to my model with .stan extension removed>

As a hack, you can sneak a -g flag in there:

    make O="0 -g" <path to my model with .stan extension removed>

On Windows, you'll have to use O="1 -g", as an optimization level of 0 causes problems compiling.
